nodes.title: Groundwork for Neural Network-Based Specific Emitter Identification Authentication for IoT
nodes.methodology: Neural networks (NNs) are used for specific emitter identification (SEI) by analyzing raw in-phase and quadrature (IQ) streams. Protocols are proposed to secure IoT networks, with a focus on low-latency, lightweight authentication.
nodes.contribution: This work establishes the foundation for using NN-based SEI for IoT authentication, emphasizing low-cost, low-power, and low-latency multi-factor authentication through RF fingerprinting.

nodes.title: A Self-supervised Framework for Generalized RF Fingerprinting and Zero-shot Anomaly Detection in Dynamic IoT Networks
nodes.methodology: A self-supervised framework combining domain-informed augmentation (DIA) and multi-task contrastive pretraining with shallow-to-medium CNN fine-tuning, optimized for contrastive temperature (τ ≈ 0.1) and learning rate (1×10⁻³).
nodes.contribution: Unifies physics-informed multi-category augmentation with multi-task contrastive pretraining for generalized fingerprinting and zero-shot anomaly detection under data scarcity and domain shifts.

nodes.dataset: 4 Zigbee devices with 60,000 samples each (1000 sampling points per sample).
nodes.methodology: Proposes a lightweight CNN model for radio frequency fingerprinting identification (RFFID) to reduce power consumption and cost while maintaining high accuracy.
nodes.contribution: Introduces a lightweight CNN-based RFFID method for Zigbee with low power consumption and high accuracy.

nodes.title: Radio Transmitter Fingerprinting: A Steady State Frequency Domain Approach
nodes.dataset: Eight identical USRP transmitters tested at 30dB and 0dB SNR. Preambles from UMTS RACH channels with 1MHz bandwidth and 4096 chips at 0.768Mcps.
nodes.methodology: Combines frequency domain analysis with k-NN classifiers to exploit steady-state signal features. Uses USRP transmitters to capture and analyze preambles, normalizing time-domain samples and extracting log-spectral-energy features.
nodes.contribution: Proposes steady-state frequency domain analysis with classifiers for RF fingerprinting, offering better performance than transient-based techniques and enabling scalable transmitter identification.

nodes.title: Improving Wireless Network Security Based On Radio Fingerprinting
nodes.dataset: 10 Motorola walkie-talkies for signal collection and identification.
nodes.methodology: Fractional Fourier Transform (FrFT) for transient signal feature extraction, Robust Principal Component Analysis (RPCA) for dimensionality reduction, and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) for classification.
nodes.contribution: Proposed a novel radio frequency fingerprint extraction method combining FrFT, RPCA, and KNN for secure wireless device identification.
